correctness.rationale: For uniformly bounded peripheral clique sizes s_i<=M and S=sum s_i->infinity with S/r-log S->c, fixing the hub color makes each clique a uniform injection from the r other colors and leaves the blocks independent. Every peripheral vertex has a clique for its open neighborhood, hence only the hub needs a singleton nonhub color. For fixed j target colors, the absent probability multiplies to exp(-jS/r+o(1)); distinct-block placements give (S/r)^j and same-block collisions are relatively O(1/S), since S/r^2->0. Thus E[(X)_j]->exp(-jc) for each fixed j and factorial-moment convergence proves Poisson(exp(-c)) and PCF success 1-exp(-exp(-c)). Inclusion-exclusion finite coefficient formula properly accounts for all named colors and disjoint block assignments. I independently checked exact proper-coloring counts in four small bouquet configurations; these finite tests do not prove the asymptotic assertion.
residual_risks: Fixed uniform maximum block size M, S->infinity, critical scaling S/r-log S->c only.
Finite independent checks cover four examples, not all graphs/asymptotic cases.
